nodes.question: How does functional connectivity relate to habitat availability and quality?
nodes.answer: Functional connectivity is expected to increase with greater habitat availability and quality across the landscape, regardless of whether habitats are structurally connected or not.
nodes.paragraph: conservation interventionsshould strive to increase habitat quality (Better), habitat size (Bigger), habitat quantity across the wider landscape (More), and nally connectivity (Joined) (Lawton et al.2010 ). Combined, these components promote resilient ecological networks for the conservation of multiple spe- cies in the long term, while the order BBMJ re ects theseparate components relative importance for population viability at the landscape scale (Isaac et al. 2018 ). Habitat features such as patch size, habitat amount, quality, frag-mentation, and connectivity, have been shown to affect ecological processes determining population viability in various ways (MacArthur and Wilson 1967 ; Hanski 1999 ; Fahrig 2003 ; Hodgson et al. 2011 ). The review by Hodgson et al. ( 2011 ) suggests that, especially with a changing cli- mate, habitat area and quality are of primary importancethrough their effect on population size and reproduction, enhancing both long-term persistence of local populations and the production of the propagules that can bene t fromenhanced connectivity. Furthermore, functional connec- tivity, i.e. the connectedness of local populations through movement and dispersal between different parts of alandscape, is expected to increase with an increasing habitat availability and quality across the landscape, whe- ther habitats are structurally connected or not (Hodgsonet al.

nodes.question: Why is further research on improving the connection between nature and people deemed necessary?
nodes.answer: Further research is required as it could be key to achieving sustainability.
nodes.paragraph: In this context, it is widely accepted that people S connectedness to nature, meaning the extent to which humans see themselves as part of the natural environment, is positively associated with greater concern and empa - thy for nature. Being more connected to nature promotes pro-ecological behaviour, awakening a sense of responsibility and care towards the environment, as well as entailing several other associated benefits, such as people S health, well-being, or hap - piness (Mayer & Frantz, 2004 ; Mayer et al., 2009 ; Schultz, 2001 ). Further research is required on how the connection between nature and people can be improved, since this could be regarded as key to achieving sustainability (Riechers et al., 2021 ). Schultz ( 2002 was one of the first to define the connectedness to nature construct as the extent to which an individual includes nature within his/her cognitive repre - sentation of self (p. 67). Currently, connectedness to nature could be regarded as a very broad construct that encompasses different aspects. According to Tam ( 2013 ), the same concept is referred to in different ways by different authors and, similarly, there are numerous tools to measure connectedness to nature or something concep - tually related (Barragan-Jason et al., 2022 ; Frantz & Mayer, 2014 ).
